item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 202335
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
500 PM PDT Sun Sep 20 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Storm Odalys, located located over a thousand miles west-southwest
of the southern tip of Baja California, and on newly formed Tropical
Depression Seventeen-E, located a few hundred miles south of
Manzanillo, Mexico.

East-Southeast of the Hawaiian Islands (Former TD 15-E):
Showers and thunderstorms have increased, but remain disorganized,
in association with the remnants of Tropical Depression Fifteen-E,
located more than 500 miles to the east-southeast of the Hawaiian
Islands. Environmental conditions are forecast to become more
conducive for development of this system by the middle to latter
portion of this week, and a tropical depression is likely to form by
that time to the south or southeast of the Hawaiian Islands as the
system moves generally westward at 10 to 15 mph.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...70 percent.

South of the Gulf of Tehuantepec:
An area of low pressure could form in a few days to the south of the
Gulf of Tehuantepec. Thereafter, environmental conditions appear
favorable for gradual development while the system moves slowly
west-northwestward to northwestward, parallel to the coast of
southern and southwestern Mexico.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...low...20 percent.

&&
Public Advisories on Tropical Storm Odalys are issued under WMO
header WTPZ31 KNHC and under AWIPS header MIATCPEP1.
Forecast Advisories on Tropical Storm Odalys are issued under WMO
header WTPZ21 KNHC and under AWIPS header MIATCMEP1.

Public Advisories on Tropical Depression Seventeen-E are issued
under WMO header WTPZ32 KNHC and under AWIPS header MIATCPEP2.
Forecast/Advisories on Tropical Depression Seventeen-E are issued
under WMO header WTPZ22 KNHC and under AWIPS header MIATCMEP2.

$$
Forecaster Papin

----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...13.1N 127.7W

PRESENT MOVEMENT...NW OR 310 DEGREES AT 13 MPH...20 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...1002 MB...29.59 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 800 PM PDT (0300 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Odalys was
located near latitude 13.1 North, longitude 127.7 West. Odalys is
moving toward the northwest near 13 mph (20 km/h), and an abrupt 
turn toward the east is expected on Tuesday.  A gradual turn toward 
the east-northeast is expected by the middle part of the week 
followed by a turn toward the northeast by the end of the week.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 50 mph (85 km/h) with higher gusts.
Gradual strengthening is expected to resume on Monday, and Odalys 
is forecast to become a hurricane by mid-week.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 70 miles (110 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 1002 mb (29.59 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
None
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 200 AM PDT.
 
$$
Forecaster Roberts

item.title: Tropical Storm Odalys Forecast Discussion Number 4
item.description:
Issued at 800 PM PDT Sun Sep 20 2026 
000
WTPZ41 KNHC 210242
TCDEP1
 
Tropical Storm Odalys Discussion Number   4
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP162026
800 PM PDT Sun Sep 20 2026
 
The northerly shear that has been impeding Odalys' intensification 
rate appears to have increased during the past several hours.  The 
surface center has become exposed to the northwest of the deep 
convective cloud mass, and the cloud tops have warmed somewhat as 
well.  The UW-CIMSS objective intensity estimates and the TAFB 
Dvorak satellite intensity classification yield an intensity of 45 
kt for this advisory.
 
Although Odalys is moving over warm oceanic temperatures and within 
a moist, unstable air mass, modest northerly vertical shear should 
continue to impinge on the northern side of the cyclone for the next 
24 hours. Consequently, little if any strengthening is expected in 
the short-term. By Monday evening, the SHIPS statistical intensity 
model and the global models show the shear diminishing, allowing 
Odalys to strengthen through day 4 gradually. Afterward, increasing 
deep-layer shear and less favorable thermodynamic atmospheric 
conditions are expected to inhibit further intensification and 
commence a slow weakening trend. The official intensity forecast 
indicates a slower rate of strengthening compared to the previous 
one, and is very close to the HCCA and GDMI aids, but above the IVCN 
consensus guidance. 
 
Odalys' initial motion is estimated to be northwestward, or 310/11 
kt, and this general motion should continue through Monday night.  
On Tuesday, a rather abrupt turn toward the east is forecast in 
response to a mid- to upper-level amplifying tropospheric trough 
moving over the eastern Pacific toward the west coast of California 
and the Baja California peninsula.  By mid-week, the cyclone should 
gradually move east-northeastward and eventually northeastward 
within the weakness created by the trough and in the northwestern 
side of a mid-level ridge situated between Odalys and Tropical Storm 
Polo.  The NHC track forecast lies between the HFIP HCCA and the 
GDMI TC ensemble mean and is adjusted to the right of the previous 
forecast beyond day 3.

item.description:

NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP172026

...DEPRESSION BECOMES TROPICAL STORM POLO...
...FORECAST TO RAPIDLY INTENSIFY INTO A MAJOR HURRICANE...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 900 PM CST...0300 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...15.1N 104.6W
ABOUT 270 MI...435 KM S OF MANZANILLO MEXICO
ABOUT 270 MI...430 KM SW OF ZIHUATANEJO MEXICO
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...40 MPH...65 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...ENE OR 75 DEGREES AT 5 MPH...7 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...1004 MB...29.65 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
Interests along the southwestern coast of Mexico should monitor the
progress of this system.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 900 PM CST (0300 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Polo was 
located near latitude 15.1 North, longitude 104.6 West. Polo is now 
moving toward the east-northeast near 5 mph (7 km/h). A turn toward 
the east is expected on Tuesday, followed by a decrease in forward 
speed and a sharp turn toward the north and northwest on Wednesday.
 
Maximum sustained winds have increased to near 40 mph (65 km/h) 
with higher gusts. Rapid intensification is forecast over the next 
few days, and Polo is expected to become a major hurricane by the 
middle part of the week. 
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 45 miles (75 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 1004 mb (29.65 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
Key messages for Tropical Storm Polo can be found in the Tropical 
Cyclone Discussion under AWIPS header MIATCDEP2 and WMO header 
WTPZ42 KNHC.
 
RAINFALL: Tropical Storm Polo is expected to produce rainfall totals 
of 4 to 8 inches, with isolated maximum totals up to 12 inches 
across coastal portions of the Mexican states of Michoacán, Colima, 
and Jalisco through Thursday. This rainfall may produce 
life-threatening flooding and mudslides, especially in areas of 
steep terrain.

For a complete depiction of forecast rainfall associated with 
Tropical Storm Polo, please see the National Weather Service Storm 
Total Rainfall Graphic available at 
hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep2.shtml?rainqpf
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 300 AM CST.
 
$$
Forecaster Papin

item.title: Tropical Depression Seventeen-E Forecast Discussion Number 1
item.description:
Issued at 300 PM CST Sun Sep 20 2026 
000
WTPZ42 KNHC 202058
TCDEP2
 
Tropical Depression Seventeen-E Discussion Number   1
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP172026
300 PM CST Sun Sep 20 2026

The tropical disturbance to the south of Mexico, formerly Invest 
99E, has become better organized with some convective banding 
features over its eastern semicircle.  Although a recent 
scatterometer pass missed the circulation, low cloud motions 
indicate that the system now has enough of a low-level circulation 
to qualify as a tropical depression with an initial intensity of 30 
kt this advisory. 

The center has been difficult to track so far so the initial motion 
is a rather uncertain 030/7 kt.  According to the majority of the 
track guidance, the system is likely to turn eastward within the 
next 12 to 24 hours.  This motion is apparently due to the system 
being embedded within a broader cyclonic gyre near the southern 
coast of Mexico.  Later in the forecast period, the system is 
expected to turn toward the northwest and move on the southern side 
of a mid-level high.  The official forecast is near the northern 
side of the track guidance model envelope.

The depression should be situated within an environment that is 
conducive for strengthening during the next few days, with very 
light vertical wind shear, and very warm sea surface temperatures.  
The official intensity forecast is near the model consensus and 
shows the system becoming a hurricane in 36 h.  It should be noted 
that the Google DeepMind and HCCA guidance call for even faster 
strengthening than shown in this initial forecast.


Key Messages:
1. Heavy rainfall associated with Tropical Depression 17-E will 
impact coastal portions of southwest Mexico this week. This rainfall 
may produce life-threatening flooding and mudslides, especially in 
areas of steep terrain.

2. Tropical Depression 17-E is forecast to strengthen and move 
closer to the southwestern Mexican coast as a major hurricane later 
this week. Although it is too soon to determine the exact location 
or magnitude of impacts associated with the system, interest in 
Mexico should closely monitor its progress and updates to the 
forecast.
